questions.q: What was the reverse psychology Hisham used?
options: Making Zuhayr feel guilty by contrasting his comfort with the besieged relatives
questions.explain: Hisham built an argument and assembled a front.

questions.q: Why did Hakim bin Hizam send food although not yet a Muslim?
options: He did good even before being Muslim, though he was threatened

questions.q: What is meant by having the courage to be the first?
options: Change begins with one stubborn person who finds a way and persuades others
questions.explain: Zuhayr, Hisham and others started it.

questions.q: What was Abu Jahal's title in Makkah because of his cleverness?
questions.explain: Abul Hakam was Abu Jahal's title.

questions.q: How did the sacred month help the Prophet SAW?
options: Killing was forbidden, so he could go out and meet people
questions.explain: The sacred month was a season of safety.

questions.q: Non-Muslims also endured because of tribal ties and principles of justice.
Hisham just raged at Abu Jahal with no strategy.
questions.explain: False. Hisham organised arguments and built a line.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Rising at the Kaaba against the agreement
The boycott is hung in the Kaaba

questions.explain: They gathered in the Shi'b, the boycott was hung, opponents rose, termites ate it and the document was torn up.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: A traitor who collaborates with the enemy
A total economic and social blockade
Abu Talib's valley squeezed between mountains

questions.explain: The boycott is a total blockade, the shi'b is a valley, a collaborator is a traitor, and an enemy within ruins unity from inside.

questions.q: Without pressure we easily forget the big picture and quarrel over small things. What is the danger?
options: The danger of being too comfortable
questions.explain: Be mindful on seeing others' trials.
